questions.q: How did Stephen King handle rejection slips?
a: He pinned them to a nail and kept submitting
He stopped writing for several years
He sent angry letters to the editors
He paid magazines to publish his stories
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes King pinning rejection slips to a nail and replacing it when the nail fell out.

questions.q: Why does King advise avoiding adverbs?
a: They pull focus from the action and reveal weak writing
They make sentences too short to understand
They are considered old-fashioned grammar
They confuse readers about who is speaking
questions.why: Lesson 2 says adverbs take focus from the action and often disguise a lack of confidence.

questions.q: Which sentence does King use as an example of weak passive voice?
a: The football was thrown by Francis
Francis threw the ball with all his might
After shuffling her feet, Bertha admitted it
Bertha timidly admitted she ate the candy
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts the passive football sentence with the direct active version.

questions.q: What daily writing habit does King recommend to beginners?
a: About 1,000 words a day, six days a week
One flawless page every morning
A few lines whenever inspiration strikes
Eight hours of writing every single day
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends a fixed place and time, aiming for 1,000 words a day six days a week.

questions.q: Why does King say writers must read a lot?
a: It shapes your taste, style and sense of what works
It guarantees your first book will sell
It removes the need for any feedback
It lets you copy successful authors exactly
questions.why: Lesson 3 says studying other writers teaches you what good writing is and helps form your own style.
